inspiration: The repo has no art. Its value is the data design: NPC, spawn, loot and rules tables kept as SQL, with named rule toggles (e.g. charm and augment enforcement). Build our own tuning as named toggles with notes.
Companion characters (mercenaries and bots) get their own spell lists per class and proficiency. Idea to recreate: a hireable companion with its own spells and stances, with our names and roles.
A salvage recipe path exists where items break into components; an update later cleans up the salvage entries. Idea: a salvage loop that turns unwanted gear into our own materials.
Augment rules (slot restriction and usability enforcement) show a socketed-gear idea: add-ons that a slot must accept. Recreate with our own socket shapes and our own rules.
Bard-style out-of-combat songs are set as spell entries on bot NPCs. Idea: an out-of-combat buff loop for companions, with our own audio and names.
The server is split into separate world, zone, login and query services in their own folders. This is an architecture idea for our own service boundaries, not an asset.

briefs.label: Hireable companion
briefs.why: A companion with its own spell list and gear makes a party feel bigger without extra players.
briefs.keep: Per-class spell list; stance per companion; companion gear slots
briefs.change: Our own roles, names and abilities; a different hire model; our own companion silhouettes

briefs.label: Salvage loop
briefs.why: Gives unwanted gear a second use and gives crafting a sink.
briefs.keep: Gear that breaks into components; cleanup of salvage recipes
briefs.change: Our own material types and salvage rules; a different breakdown result per item class

briefs.label: Socketed add-on gear
briefs.why: Slot-based add-ons give loot a build decision without new items.
briefs.keep: Slot restriction; usability check; named rule toggle
briefs.change: Our own socket shapes and add-on types; our own enforcement rules
